titel: Your first order step by step
kurz: Which five details determine the price of an order, and why the largest cost item does not appear in any fee table.

bloecke.md:
An order is an offer to enter into a contract, even if it is sent at the push of a button. It consists of five details: which security, on which trading venue, what quantity, on what condition and how long the offer is to remain valid. The other fields of the order form are secondary.

The fee gets talked about the most, and it is the easiest to compare. The execution price, by contrast, does not appear as a cost item in any breakdown. It results from the choice of trading venue, time of day and order type, and for larger amounts it is usually the bigger item.

schritte.text: Take the ISIN from the factsheet or the issuer's website rather than from the results list of the search function. Then check: distributing or accumulating, the currency of the quotation, and for foreign shares whether it is the original share or a depositary receipt.

schritte.titel: Choose the trading venue and time
schritte.text: If in doubt, choose the reference market during core trading hours. Trade securities with US underlyings only after 15:30, when the underlying shares are also being traded.

Enter the number of units or the amount, and for bonds the face value. The number of units is the amount divided by the ask price. If the amount is calculated too tightly, the order will be rejected for lack of cover if the price rises.

schritte.titel: Set the order type and limit
schritte.text: When buying, set the limit just above the ask price, and when selling, just below the bid price. Use market orders only when the order book is deep and the reference market is open.
The most sensible setting is “valid for the day”. If the limit is still to apply the next day, it is then set again, in the light of the new prices.
Before the order is sent, the broker must disclose the costs. The disclosure includes fees and charges, but not the trading spread, because this is contained in the price.

Compare the execution price with the reference price for the same minute, check the number of units and the fees, and report anything unusual immediately. The deadlines for cancelling a trade are short.

bloecke.md:
## The ISIN as a unique identifier

The ISIN has twelve characters. It consists of two letters for the country code, nine characters for the national identifier and a check digit. The country code stands for the jurisdiction of the security and not for the company. An ETF on US shares with an identifier beginning IE… is therefore an Irish fund and not a US product. The six-character WKN is the older German securities identification number and continues to be used alongside it.

The most common source of error with a first order is searching by name. Under the same index name you will often find a distributing and an accumulating share class, a currency-hedged variant, an older share class with a higher fee and the same share class on several exchanges in different currencies. With foreign shares, a depositary receipt (ADR) with its own ratio and annual custody fees charged by the depositary bank often appears instead of the share. In the search results, these entries look almost identical.

bloecke.md:
Xetra trades continuously from 9:00 to 17:30. In addition, there is an opening auction, an intraday auction and a closing auction, which for securities in the DAX, MDAX and SDAX is followed by five minutes of trading at the closing auction price. In continuous trading, price-time priority applies, so the better limit is executed first and, where limits are equal, the older order. An extended retail service also covers 8:00 to 8:55 and 17:30 to 22:00.

All other German venues trade beyond Xetra core hours, but not necessarily on better terms. On these venues, which are also exchanges, a specialist or market maker sets the bid and ask prices itself; there is no order book with many participants there. As long as the reference market is open, the market maker takes its cue from the prices there. When the reference market is closed, it bears the news risk alone and gets paid for this through a wider spread.

With a world ETF that has a high US weighting, there is the additional factor that the fund's largest positions are not traded in the morning and their price is only estimated. The [[iNAV]] is recalculated every 15 to 60 seconds and serves market makers as a guide, but during this time it is itself based on estimates. From 15:30, when the US exchanges open, spreads are typically at their narrowest.

bloecke.titel: Price certainty and execution certainty of order types
bloecke.unter: Schematic. The top right corner remains empty, because price certainty and execution certainty pull in opposite directions and every order form demands a choice between them.

felder.text: Execution practically certain, price open. Justifiable only with a deep order book and while the reference market is trading.
There is no order that guarantees both execution and price. With a limit, the price is secured, but execution is not.
The market decides whether the order is triggered and at what price it is then traded.
Price limited, execution uncertain. The sensible standard case for private investors.

bloecke.md:
In German order forms, a market order is labelled “billigst” (at the lowest price) when buying and “bestens” (at the best price) when selling. Both words are misleading. They mean immediate execution at any available price, not the best price. The order is executed against the offers in the order book and, if little is on offer, also reaches into the second and third price levels. Deutsche Börse's investor portal shows ten price levels per side for Xetra; offers further down are not visible there. This is another reason why large market orders become so expensive in thin order books.

A limit order sets a price limit: a maximum price when buying and a minimum price when selling. The drawback is that execution is not certain. If the order is also meant to be executed, the limit belongs just above the ask price or just below the bid price, and not 2% away from the market. Execution is then very likely, and the protection against outliers is still preserved.

bloecke.md:
A stop-loss order does not guarantee a sale at the stop price. When the price touches the threshold, it is converted into a market order and executed at the next tradable price. If the share opens with a price gap of 20% after a profit warning, it is sold at the bottom end of the gap and not at the stop price.

On 6 May 2010, the S&P 500 fell by a further 5% to 6% within around four minutes, and the Dow Jones at times by more than 9% (around 1,000 points). Between 14:40 and 15:00 New York time, around 2 billion shares changed hands. Triggered stop-loss orders were executed at prices that were no longer being traded minutes later. The regulators responded with circuit breakers. On Xetra, the [[Volatility interruption|volatility interruption]] of at least 120 seconds performs the same function.

A stop-limit order does limit the execution price, but in a crash it may not be executed at all. It therefore replaces one risk with another. In addition, a stop on a trading venue with a market maker can be triggered at night by a brief widening of the spread, even though nothing has happened on the reference market.

## Validity and partial execution

Validity is the detail that is least often set deliberately. An order valid for the day expires to the extent that it has not been executed by the close of trading on the relevant trading venue. Longer periods are possible depending on the trading venue and broker, usually limited to the end of a month or year. A limit order that sits in the order book for weeks is an open offer to the market. If bad news arrives at some point, this order is the first to be executed.

If there is not enough volume on the other side at the limit, a [[Partial execution|partial execution]] occurs. Technically this is unproblematic, but not always in terms of cost. If the broker charges per day of execution, the same order executed over three days triggers fees three times. With a flat fee of one euro this does not matter, but with a percentage commission subject to a minimum amount it does. For thinly traded securities, it therefore pays to look at the list of prices and services. Where the broker offers it, the condition of same-day or complete execution can also be useful.

bloecke.titel: Fee and spread by order size
bloecke.unter: Illustrative calculation with a fixed flat order fee of €1. Up to about €5,000 the fee weighs more heavily, above that the trading spread. Outside core hours, the spread almost always dominates.

serien.name: Flat order fee of €1 (as % of volume)
Half spread 0.02% (Xetra core hours, large ETF)

bloecke.md:
In an illustrative calculation, an investor invests €2,000 in a large world ETF via Xetra at 15:45. The bid price is 99.98 and the ask price 100.02. This corresponds to a spread of 0.04%, the order of magnitude reported for the largest world ETFs during core hours.

- When buying at the ask price, the half spread relative to the mid price costs 0.02%, that is, €0.40.
- The flat order fee (assumed to be €1) corresponds to 0.05%.
- Together this comes to €1.40 or 0.07%.

If the same order is placed at 8:15 on a trading venue with a market maker where the spread at that time is assumed to be 0.20%, the half spread costs €2.00. With the flat fee of €1, the total is €3.00. Both contract notes show the same fee. The difference of €1.60 does not appear anywhere as a cost item; it only shows up in the worse purchase price.

With twelve such purchases a year, that amounts to €19.20. Measured against an annual investment of €24,000, this corresponds to 0.08% and thus around 40% of what a world ETF with a management fee of 0.20% costs on the same sum in the same year. And this is solely about the choice of time and trading venue.

bloecke.md:
With bonds, you order a face value instead of a number of units, and the price is quoted as a percentage of face value. An order for €3,000 nominal at a price of 96.40 costs €2,892, plus [[Accrued interest|accrued interest]] for the period since the last coupon payment. The quoted price is the clean price without accrued interest; the settlement amount corresponds to the dirty price. That is why the amount debited is higher than the price alone would suggest.

Then there is the minimum denomination. With German federal bonds, small amounts can be traded, whereas with many corporate bonds the smallest tradable unit is €100,000 nominal. For a private portfolio, such securities are in practice only accessible through a fund.

An executed trade is final. On the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, cancellation because of an obviously non-market price ([[Mistrade|mistrade]]) can only be applied for within 30 minutes of receipt of the trade confirmation for Xetra transactions, and within two trading hours in specialist trading on Börse Frankfurt. For shares on Xetra, the price must also deviate from the fair market price by at least 5% and by at least €0.50. If the contract note is only read at the weekend, the deadline has usually passed.

Open limit orders are usually deleted from the order book in the event of corporate actions and on the day of the ex-dividend markdown, because the price makes an arithmetical jump. A limit that is to remain in force must be entered again.

The standard order for private investors is a limit order during the core hours of the reference market. Market orders are the exception and are suitable only for very liquid securities at times when many participants are active in the order book.

- A **fill-or-kill order** (FOK) is executed immediately and in full, or not at all.
- With **immediate-or-cancel** (IOC), as much as possible is executed immediately and the rest lapses.
- With an **iceberg order**, only part of the volume is visible in the order book. It only makes sense for sizes that would move the market by themselves.
- The **one-cancels-other** combination links two orders so that execution of one deletes the other, typically a price target and a stop.

Which of these conditions are available depends on the trading venue and the broker and differs considerably between neobrokers and direct banks. Investors who need them should check this before opening a securities account.

mitnehmen: An order consists of five decisions, and the most expensive part is the combination of trading venue, time of day and order type, not the fee.
Execution certainty and price certainty are mutually exclusive; the sensible standard case is the limit order during the core hours of the reference market.
When triggered, a stop-loss becomes a market order and therefore does not protect against price gaps; a stop-limit replaces this risk with the risk of non-execution.
For small amounts the fixed fee predominates, and from about €5,000 the trading spread.
The contract note should be checked right after execution, because errors must be reported within hours and the trade is final after that.

begriffe.text: Combination of a trigger threshold and a price limit. When the price reaches the stop, a limit order is created instead of a market order. It protects against execution at outlier prices, but in a crash it may not be executed at all.
Stop order whose threshold follows the price upwards at a fixed absolute or percentage distance and stays put when prices fall. Once triggered, the order is executed at the next tradable price.
Execution of an order in several tranches because there is not enough volume on the other side at the desired limit. Depending on the fee model, it can trigger costs more than once.
Automatic switch from continuous trading to an auction when the potential price leaves the permitted corridor. On Xetra it lasts at least 120 seconds. It prevents executions at outlier prices.
Trade concluded at an obviously non-market price. Cancellation is only possible within short deadlines and above a minimum deviation from the fair market price.
